keyFindings.description: The advertiser (line 358) runs `/bin/sh -c` as its container's PID 1 with no SIGTERM trap. Linux delivers a signal to a PID namespace's init only when init has a handler for it (pid_namespaces(7)), so the kubelet's SIGTERM is dropped, and each front-door pod's termination runs to the 60 s grace and SIGKILL. Fix: trap 'exit 0' TERM and `sleep N & wait $!`, plus a test that fails without them. Take INFRA-549's fix (its commit 8bf4bfe7, not on origin at 08:35Z) byte for byte, since the file is shared. Raised by the INFRA-63 architect from INFRA-549's review. A local unshare test on this gVisor host did not reproduce the drop, so it is no evidence either way.
cert-publish (dispatchCertPublishLoop, lines 211-221) has the same PID 1 shape: no TERM trap, and a foreground `sleep 60`.

'Notes for the window (INFRA-561)' leaves out the client grant to svc:<hostname> on 443 (or a Service tag) and the tcp:443 port that README.md:172-183 and move step 1 require. The census's tailscale-state row does not list docs/plans/2026-10-14-dispatch-gcp-plan.md.
The proof's observed text says cert-publish exits 'within 30 s' of the gate dying. The loop checks once a pass and each pass ends in `sleep 60`, so the tester measured 57.5-59 s.
Lines 678-682 do not say that while cert-publish restarts after its gate dies, the pod is not ready and leaves the SOCKS5 Service even though it still hosts the Tailscale Service.
Hardening: kube() (line 197) runs curl with no --max-time, so a stuck request keeps the gate alive to kill -0 while it decides nothing. Add --max-time 20.
